brief: Three bases arranged around an empty spot, with a bay tray standing in that spot.

requirements.requirement: Three bases arranged around an empty spot
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (2,0,0) surround the empty cell (1,1,0). Each of the three touches it. The original base at (0,0,0) was removed so the spot stays empty.

requirements.requirement: A bay tray standing in that spot
requirements.evidence: Bay bay:0#1,1#bay1 (hex-bin-bay-n-full-solid, a full north bay tray) is notched into the empty cell (1,1,0), bolted to the three bases.

finish.summary: Built three hex bases at (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (2,0,0) around the empty cell (1,1,0), with a full bay tray seated in that cell. The first try used a cell with only two neighbours, so I moved the third base. Ran capOpenFaces and lockJoints, which added 11 end caps and 2 joint bolts. check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
